title: Juniper and the Alibi
premise: When twin letters arrive at the office of coroner Sebastian Winterbourne — one confessing to a twenty-year-old drowning, one promising a second death unless she decodes a ledger hidden in the town's own records — Sebastian discovers the victim was her late mother's closest friend, and the confession is signed in her mother's handwriting. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Sebastian must untangle a cipher woven into gravestone epitaphs and burial ledgers, aided by an unlikely found family: a retired archivist, a teenage gravedigger, and the confessor's estranged daughter. The trail leads to a cover-up that protected the town's founding families, and to a final revelation that forces Sebastian to choose between exposing the truth and preserving the loyalty of the only family she has left. In the end, she publishes the decoded ledger, closes the case on her own terms, and gains a family built on honesty rather than silence.
about_author: Marguerite Ishikawa spent a decade cataloguing small-town archives across the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction, a habit that still shows in her obsession with paper trails. She writes mysteries about people who keep records because memory alone cannot be trusted.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Sebastian Winterbourne's POV. A quiet morning among the town's familiar dead is shattered when two letters arrive: a full confession to a 2004 drowning, and a threat promising another death in thirty days. The signature on both matches her deceased mother's handwriting. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in disbelief.

chapters.title: The Drowning Nobody Drowned
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She pulls the old case file on Elodie Marsh, whose death was ruled accidental, and finds her mother was the last person to see her alive. Flashbacks establish their mothers' friendship. Emotional beat: grief reopening like a wound.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with interludes from teen gravedigger Theo. Walking the cemetery for clues, Sebastian notices Elodie's epitaph doesn't match the ledger entry. Theo mentions someone visited the grave last week. Emotional beat: first spark of purpose.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Bargain
chapters.summary: Retired archivist Odile Chen's POV. Odile agrees to help decode discrepancies but extracts a promise: whatever they find, nothing gets buried again. Her history with the founding families hints at old wounds. Emotional beat: wary alliance formed.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Comparing fifty years of burial ledgers against headstones, the team finds systematic mismatches — dates shifted by days, initials transposed. It's not sloppiness; it's a cipher. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Daughter
chapters.summary: Nadia Voss's POV. Nadia arrives in town hunting whoever sent the letters, believing they implicate her father, the former sheriff. She and Sebastian circle each other with mutual suspicion. Emotional beat: two investigations colliding.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, Twenty-Nine Left
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A second letter arrives early, narrowing the deadline and naming a new target: Odile. The threat proves the sender knows their every move. Emotional beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: What the Statute Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile explains the legal clock: prosecute now or never. She reveals the founding families' consortium once owned everything, including the coroner's office. Emotional beat: the scale of the conspiracy becomes real.

chapters.title: Transposed Initials
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo cracks the first cipher layer — initials map to names of consortium members. One name stuns them all: W. Winterbourne. Sebastian's mother was inside the machine. Emotional beat: betrayal by the dead.

chapters.title: Mother's Marginalia
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Searching her mother's belongings, Sebastian finds annotated newspaper clippings and a half-burned photograph of Elodie alive after her supposed death date. Emotional beat: hope that mother was a whistleblower, not a killer.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Doubt
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia confronts her dying father; his rambling denial contains one damning detail only a participant would know. She switches sides, bringing his old case notes to Sebastian. Emotional beat: loyalty shifting toward truth.

chapters.title: Fifteen Days: The Quiet Threat
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Someone ransacks the archive room; the original 2004 file is gone. Theo catches a glimpse of the intruder — wearing a coroner's department jacket. Emotional beat: the enemy is inside.

chapters.title: Deputy of Old Ghosts
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. The current sheriff, once her father's deputy, acts helpful while steering them wrong. Nadia plays along, feeding him false progress. Emotional beat: dangerous cat-and-mouse confidence.

chapters.title: Epitaph Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile realizes the epitaphs encode dates of payments — hush money routed through the cemetery trust. The final epitaph, unfinished, points to a grave that doesn't exist yet. Emotional beat: horror dawning — the promised death has a reserved plot.

chapters.title: Ten Days: The Empty Plot
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They locate the pre-purchased plot under a shell name. Whoever dies will be buried as 'E.M.' — the sender intends to complete Elodie's story with a real corpse. Emotional beat: stakes turn mortal and personal.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A hidden letter from her mother surfaces, revealing she discovered the drowning was murder, gathered evidence, and died before she could act — or was helped to die. Emotional beat: devastating clarity and fury.

chapters.title: Five Days: The Trap We Set
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The team decides to bait the sender by leaking a fake breakthrough. Theo plants the decoy ledger page; Nadia watches the sheriff's office; Sebastian waits at the empty plot. Emotional beat: terrified resolve.

chapters.title: Who Signs a Confession
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The trap springs: the sender is the town's beloved funeral director, Elodie's brother, who faked her death records to expose the consortium after failing through legal channels — and the 'second death' letter was his desperation, not intent to kill. Emotional beat: relief curdling into complication.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. With the statute expiring at midnight, the team debates: publish the decoded ledger and torch the town, or bury it and protect the living, including Sebastian's mother's reputation. Each character argues from their wound. Emotional beat: the thematic crucible.

chapters.title: Midnight Filing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the county courthouse, minutes before expiration, Sebastian files the decoded ledger and her mother's evidence, naming names — including her mother's complicity in staying silent. Emotional beat: costly, cleansing courage.

chapters.title: Requiem, Corrected
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The consortium falls; the town convulses; some friendships don't survive. Elodie's true death date is carved properly, and the funeral director attends, forgiven but not absolved. Emotional beat: grief given honest shape.

chapters.title: Juniper Blooms Anyway
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue. A year later, Sebastian, Odile, Theo, and Nadia share Sunday dinners — a found family forged by truth. Sebastian plants juniper on Elodie's corrected grave and finally writes her mother's name in the ledger of the forgiven. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
